summary: The +5 pts/week target was invented before the baseline measurement exists. Risk of flat/negative backtest is rated 'low' without evidence. Waiver urgency: season is 4 weeks in, ship waivers on ESPN projections now rather than waiting for FantasyPros. Run the backtest against real data before building anything new.

resolution: Ran backtest: platform rank currently beats actual decisions by ~3 pts/week over 3 real weeks. KR-04 baseline updated. Risk-04 moved to medium. Waiver v1 scoped to ESPN projections with FantasyPros as pluggable upgrade. Scope updated to reflect pluggable projection architecture.

summary: The five contexts are the archetype's lifecycle sentence renamed, not a cut derived from the events: all five relationships are customer-supplier in one straight line, with no ACL against ESPN's undocumented write API and no shared kernel. Decision Analysis packs three aggregates with different invariants and different hard deadlines. Recommendation is a presentation layer promoted to a context. Also missing: no events after a trade offer is sent (the irreversible part), no way for a waiver claim to fail on priority (the normal outcome), no deadline-miss scenario on any journey. Concrete errors: trade packages ranked at E-105 before EV computed at E-106; AGG-backtest-report wrongly emits the DecisionLogged events.

resolution: Re-cut the contexts from the events plus code evidence. Diagnosis accepted, proposed cut rejected: three separate decision contexts would put a synchronous cross-context call inside trade evaluation, because trade_value.roster_starting_total() calls optimize_lineup() directly. Analysis stays one context with the optimizer as shared kernel; the split landed on execution instead, where invariants and deadlines actually differ and where execute/ had already split in code. Signal reclassified generic with an ACL against ESPN. Recommendation dissolved into the three execution contexts. Five of six capabilities now moved. Added the missing events: trade offer sent and resolved (accept/decline/expire, plus the stale-lineup invalidation), waiver claim submitted/cleared/lost-to-priority, and the lineup deadline miss. Fixed the ranked-before-EV inversion and the backtest aggregate wrongly claiming the decision-logged events. Added hotspots for clock-watching, offer-state visibility, and prose asserting numbers the optimizer did not compute.

summary: Trade execution is modelled as unwritable while execute/trade_api.py has sent real ESPN trade transactions since 2026-09-25 — the one irreversible action in the product, with no read-back confirmation, while the reversible lineup write has one. DECISIONS.md D-019, vision scope, and storm assumption ASM-012 are all stale against the code. Second blocker: TradeOffer identity is week+season+counterparty while an invariant says a changed offer is a new offer — a revised offer to the same manager in the same week collides, and the same defect hits LineupDecision when a mid-week trade forces a re-decide, overwriting the snapshot the replay guarantee needs. Also: 'recorded' is both mid-flight and terminal; waiver claim identity keys on a null player on the hold path; three commands still name the aggregates that were split; the brief-cannot-invent-numbers risk is the only open hotspot with no invariant; the counterparty pitch is a value object but exists for attribution.

resolution: Confirmed against the code: execute/trade_api.py POSTs real ESPN trade transactions behind dry-run and a typed LIVE prompt, and returns success on any non-4xx without reading the league back. Model corrected throughout — trade execution restated as writable-and-irreversible in contexts, the storm assumption fixed, the vision scope split into lineup and trade writes, and a read-back confirmation invariant added (I-23) plus a hotspot for the code not yet satisfying it (H-09). Identities moved to opaque ids on all three execution aggregates: the natural tuples could not represent a revised offer, a re-decided lineup after a mid-week trade, or the hold path with no player to add. Terminal 'recorded' renamed 'closed' to separate it from the mid-flight state. Added the brief-integrity invariant that H-08 had been missing, and the rule against re-offering a refused package. Dropped the replay invariant as a test rather than a constraint. Counterparty pitch promoted to entity for attribution. Three commands repointed at the aggregates they actually write. Naming reversed on review: proposal is the agent's output, offer is the sent thing, always.

summary: The architecture documents a system it partly cannot see. The decision store has a second table, scorecards, written by db/store.py:149 — data-model.md lists one table and says the backtest report is 'not persisted as a row', which is false, and the unbacked-up-file finding therefore understates what is lost. The supervisor's risk posture (agent/supervisor.py, emitted at web/runs.py:208) is injected into every web run and appears in no aspect file, so a deterministic input to every recommendation is undocumented and unconstrained by any NFR or invariant. Two NFR citations point at the wrong line: the ESPN pacing is enforced at adapters/espn.py:113-114 not :89 (a default parameter), and the loopback bind cited as NFR-11/CTL-01 enforcement lives in the main() console script, not in create_app — running uvicorn directly binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth, so the stated control is a convenience default rather than a control. Also: web/trace.py, web/filters.py, agent/tracer.py, signals/collector.py and the Sleeper adapter's role appear in no aspect file; the waiver gap is narrower than claimed (the web run kind is already refused by name at runs_routes.py:64). ADR-001 is honest but records a behaviour that its own closing line says is unreachable; ADR-002 is a genuine decision made during this pass.

resolution: All three blocking edits applied plus the two citation fixes. Verified against code: scorecards IS a second table in decisions.db (store.py:42, written at :149) — the claim that the backtest report was not persisted was factually wrong and is corrected, including that losing the file loses the computed season record as well as the raw log. The loopback bind is a default argument inside main() (web/app.py:63) while create_app (:28) enforces nothing, so it was restated from 'the access control' to a gap: there is no access control, only one entry point whose defaults happen to be safe. Supervisor risk posture now documented as a component and a cross-cutting concern — a deterministic value that shifts what the agent weighs was invisible to the architecture. Six undocumented components added (supervisor, tracer, collector, trade preferences, SSE transport) and Sleeper's purpose stated. NFR-03 re-pointed from the constructor default to the sleep that enforces it, and noted as defeasible. ADR-001 status qualified to accepted-in-principle since its thresholds do not exist, and abstention dropped as the stated ESPN-read mitigation. One correction to the challenge: the run dispatcher rejects any kind outside its worker registry rather than refusing 'waivers' by name — the test merely uses waivers as its example. Also noted the undecided case of the two SQLite files disagreeing.

summary: The walking skeleton did not walk through every layer and was three slices wearing one name: it ended at hand-typed claim instructions, stopping short of the write layer where the trade send was found returning success without acting, and it carried eight invariants while every other slice carried one to three. Its own note claimed 'one candidate considered' while requiring the closest miss and its margin, which means ranking the field. Second blocker: the sequence guaranteed the thing one of its own slices existed to prevent — the waiver filing at position 2 would have created a third copy of the LIVE gate, with the gate consolidation at position 5. Also: the measured loss is adherence rather than analysis (optimizer matched actual in weeks 1-2, was right by 8.9 in week 3 and unfollowed, naive baseline ahead by ~3/week) and the only adherence slice recorded the miss after kickoff while the pre-kickoff reminder was unscheduled. Missing entirely: a slice for the write-failure notification, the twin of the missed-recommendation failure. Dead weight: two of three risk entries on the brief-integrity slice restated the invariant instead of naming a differentiated risk. Stale: H-09 was still listed open despite shipping in f97488a.

resolution: Restructured from 10 slices to 13. Verified both checkable claims: execute/base.py:32 already declares a waiver_claim action type and the lineup write posts a ROSTER transaction, so filing by hand was a choice not a constraint; H-09 was indeed stale and is now in Resolved. Waiver slice split on the manager's decision — scoring plus logged hold ships in the October window, API filing with read-back confirmation follows and completes the skeleton. The index now states plainly that the skeleton spans two slices and why, rather than claiming one of them is it. Gate consolidation moved from position 5 to 4, ahead of the filing slice, so the waiver gate is the shared gate's first caller rather than its third copy. A pre-kickoff nudge was added at position 2 on the manager's decision, promoted above all new capability because the measured gap is adherence: the analysis was right in week 3 and unused. Its real difficulty is recorded — the tool runs on demand, so a nudge needs something that notices time passing, which is a new shape for this system. Write-failure notification added as position 8, sharing the nudge's channel rather than inventing a second. Brief-integrity risk column rewritten so each entry names a distinct exposure, with the counterparty pitch first as the real one. Slice frontmatter renumbered to match. FantasyPros kept at 13 on the manager's decision — the pluggability requirement it was really about is already met. Two gaps left deliberately unretired and now stated in the index: the decision-store schema, and two open hotspots with no slice.

summary: I-30 fully-available-roster bar may suppress useful bye-week adds; two-tier output proposed. Position held: domain invariant kept as-is, spot-start tier deferred.

resolution: Position held. I-30 kept as written. Spot-start tier recorded as a candidate future slice.
